newsitem.title: USA: Calif. legislative committee approves MTBE moratorium.
newsitem.headline: Calif. legislative committee approves MTBE moratorium.

text.p: California lawmakers on Monday moved one step closer to banning the controversial gasoline additive, MTBE, a chemical which opponents charge may cause cancer and respiratory problems.
The California Senate Environmental Quality Committee approved the bill with five votes, the minimum required.
The bill, if made law by the state assembly, would place a moratorium on the use of methyl tertiary butyl ether (MTBE) until January 1, 1999 or until the state proves the chemical is safe.
To become law, the bill must pass the Senate Appropriations Committee, the full state Senate and Assembly and be signed by the governor.
"It is unacceptable to test MTBE on 32 million Californians who are unwillingly being used as guinea pigs," the bill's author, Senator Dick Mountjoy, a Republican, said in a statement.
The bill could be extremely costly for the state's oil companies, which invested $3 billion to retool California refineries to make reformulated gasoline with MTBE.

MTBE is one of several so-called oxygenates that help make gasoline burn cleaner and allegedly cut emissions. The gasoline additive was chosen after the federal Clean Air Act of 1990 required states to improve air quality.
Opponents of the bill were not immediately available for comment.
